_clickable: every selector here is a control someone confirmed does NOT mutate — it navigates, filters, expands or dismisses. plan.py cannot check that (nothing in the markup says so), so this list IS the assertion. Adding one is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff. Never list a control that posts, votes, edits, withdraws, reports or deletes.
_clickableRepointed: 🔴 THIS LIST IS AN ASSERTION, AND IT SHRINKS AS WELL AS GROWS — `plan.py` REFUSES AN ENTRY NO STATE ACTIVATES (`clickable_unused`, exit 2 `bad_recipe`), so pruning it is mandatory rather than tidying. Last edited 2026-09-30, when the two detail states were removed and `grid-group-matchup` / `grid-col-header` went with them. ── ✅ EACH SURVIVING ENTRY WAS CONFIRMED NON-MUTATING BY READING THE SOURCE, NOT BY THE NAME. `board-nav-matchups` / `board-nav-prompts` are `<span>`s inside a `SegmentedControl` whose only handler is `onChange={(v) => onChange(v as Board)}` → `setBoard`, a `useState` in `App`. No KV write, no network, no persistence (`SideNav.tsx` states the selection is deliberately not persisted anywhere). `howto-dismiss` dismisses the explainer — see `_howToDismissal`. ── 🔴 CONTROLS DELIBERATELY *NOT* LEDGERED, AND WHY EACH IS A JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT: (a) `matchup-menu` / `prompt-menu` are the `⋮` overflow menus inside the detail modals and they contain Edit / Remove / Report. They were never ledgered and must never be — a capture may open a panel and must never touch a control inside it. (b) `grid-vote`, `grid-withdraw`, `run-cell`, `submit-matchup` and `submit-prompt` all mutate or spend; `run-cell` spends the viewer's own Buzz. (c) `grid-open`, `nav-home`, `nav-my`, `nav-my-grid|matchup|prompt`, `board-nav-grids`, `grid-group-matchup` and `grid-col-header` are all PURE VIEW SWITCHES — each was read: `grid-open` calls `onOpen(entryOpenKey(entry))` → `App`'s `setOpenGridKey`, a plain `useState` with no persistence (`git grep openGridKey` finds one `useState` and one `useMemo`, no writer); the `nav-*` items call `onSelect`/`setExpanded` only; the two grid triggers open READ-ONLY detail modals. They would be SAFE to ledger — and they are omitted anyway, because no state activates them and `clickable_unused` refuses an unused entry. 🔴 IF A FUTURE STATE USES ONE, LEDGER IT IN THE SAME EDIT.

_cropHeightTradeoff: 🔴 THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL IN THIS RECIPE, RE-DECIDED 2026-09-30 AND REVERSED, WITH THE NUMBERS THAT DECIDED IT. `crop` HAS NO PER-STATE OVERRIDE AND CANNOT BE GIVEN ONE IN A RECIPE: `capture.sh` invokes `frame.py measure <png> --recipe <recipe>` and NEVER passes the state name, so frame.py could not select a per-state rect even if one were declared. (`frame.py` does accept `--crop-rect` on its CLI, but `capture.sh` never passes it.) Per-state rects are therefore a PIPELINE change, not a recipe change — checked before choosing, so that 'one rect' is a measured constraint and not a preference. One height has to serve three states whose content differs by 174 CSS px. ── BOTH CANDIDATES WERE SHOT LIVE AND COMPARED BY EYE, not reasoned about. (a) h=1428 device (frame-CSS 1252) — REJECTED, and it is what shipped before. Every state complete, including all five `prompt-card`s. Cost: the grids and matchups assets carry 208 and 213 device px of empty app background below their last card (14.6% and 14.9% of the crop), and the crop aspect 1700/1428 = 1.19 against the 1200x778 canvas's 1.542 pillarboxes the render to 926x778 with a 137px pad each side. (b) h=1224 device (frame-CSS 1073) — SHIPPED. The grids board clears by 5px and the matchups board by 9px, so both are complete with no dead band at all; the cut lands in the gutter between the prompts board's 3rd card (ends frame-CSS 1066) and its 4th (starts 1076), so the prompts asset shows 3 of 5 prompts and no partial card. Aspect 1700/1224 = 1.39, rendering 1083x778 with a 58px pad. ── WHY (b) WON, AND WHY THE 2026-09-29 DECISION WENT THE OTHER WAY. That pass was restoring the two boards to the listing at all, and judged a complete prompts list the thing being restored. It is restored either way — the prompts asset still shows the board, its header, its submit control and its vote counts; what changes is how many rows. Against that: TWO of the three assets go from a ~15% dead band to under 1%, NONE gets structurally worse, and because the aspect moves from 1.19 to 1.39 the ink renders 1083px wide instead of 926px — every asset's content is 17% larger on the canvas, the flagship grids shot included. A voting board is a scrollable list, so three of five reads as 'there are more'; a 15% empty band on the flagship reads as a framing mistake. ── ⚠️ THE WINDOW IS SEVEN PIXELS WIDE AND BOTH EDGES ARE CONTENT: device [1220, 1227], floored by the grids board's own content bottom (1219) and ceilinged by the prompts board's 4th card (1227). 1224 is the middle. 🔴 THAT MAKES THIS A CONTENT-DEPENDENT NUMBER, NOT A LAYOUT ONE — if the crowd submits a matchup or the grids board gains a card, the floor moves and this rect starts clipping. RE-MEASURE ALL THREE BOTTOMS BEFORE ANY RE-SHOOT; do not assume 1224 still fits. ── ✅ AND THE LETTERBOX COST IS ARITHMETIC ONLY, MEASURED ON A SHIPPED ASSET RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `frame.py` pads the canvas with the SAME colour this app's background is: every pixel outside the content is rgb(26,27,30) and so is the app's own background, so there is no visible seam and no visible bar. That is why the pad percentage did not decide this and should not be quoted as a visual defect. ⚠️ IT IS A PROPERTY OF THIS APP'S DARK THEME, NOT OF THE PIPELINE: re-check it if the app ever ships a lighter surface, because then the pad WOULD show. ── 🔴 AND THE COST THIS NOTE DID NOT NAME: SHRINKING h RAISES THE SHARE OF EVERY ASSET THAT IS THE *SAME* PIXELS. The open-grid panel above the subnav is common to all three boards, so at h=1428 it was 48.6% of the frame and at h=1224 it is 56.7% — the three assets are now MORE alike, not less. `_statesRebuilt` calls near-duplicate collapse the one hazard no gate in this pipeline can see (a declared rect makes the identical-box check inert), so this trade moved the one risk nothing measures. Accepted for legibility, recorded so it is not re-derived as free.
_iframeIsViewportCapped: 🔴 THE HOST DOES NOT FIT THE IFRAME TO CONTENT, AND THAT IS WHAT DECIDES THIS RECIPE'S VIEWPORT. On the `/apps/run/<slug>` full-page surface the iframe carries inline `flex: 1 1 0%` inside a flex parent with `overflow: hidden`, so it is sized to the REMAINING VIEWPORT HEIGHT and the app's overflow is clipped by the parent. ── MEASURED AT TWO HEIGHTS, 2026-09-30: innerHeight 1100 CSS → iframe 952; innerHeight 1500 → iframe 1353. So iframe height ≈ innerHeight - 147, and ⚠️ THE 'CONSTANT' IS NOT QUITE ONE — it reads 148 at 1100 and 147 at 1500, because the iframe's own top is CSS 90.877 and its height 1352.178 and both round. Use 147 as a working figure AT THE VIEWPORT OF RECORD, not as a law, and re-measure at the height you actually intend. Iframe top is CSS 91 at both. ── THE FLOOR THAT SETS: the three boards' own content is 1091 / 1089 / 1263 CSS (grids / matchups / prompts), read off `documentElement.scrollHeight` inside the app frame AT CSS 1498x1100, where the app genuinely overflows and the number is therefore real — at the viewport of record `scrollHeight` is pinned to the iframe and says nothing. The tallest needs innerHeight ≥ 1263 + 148 = 1411 before it renders without scrolling; the viewport of record gives it 1353 of iframe against 1263 of content. ── ⚠️ WHY THE EMULATED HEIGHT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE. At CSS 1498x1100 the app overflows, a 15px space-taking scrollbar appears (clientWidth 1483 vs innerWidth 1498) AND clicking a board segment focus-scrolls the frame — measured `scrollY` 137 on the matchups board and 139 on the prompts board, from 0. A capture taken there photographs a SCROLLED app. Making the iframe taller than the content removes the scroll entirely rather than depending on where a focus-scroll happens to land. All four readings reproduced exactly on 2026-09-30. ── 🔴 THERE IS STILL NO `scroll` VERB AND THIS NOTE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR ONE. `KNOWN_ACTIONS` in `plan.py` is click / clickIfPresent / type / key / waitForText / waitForGone / trustedKey / sleep / nav, and an unknown verb is REFUSED (`bad_recipe`), never skipped. The boards are reached by making the frame taller, not by scrolling it.
_viewportOfRecord: 🔴 RE-RUNNING THIS RECIPE DOES NOT REQUIRE THE OPERATOR'S WINDOW TO BE THE ONE crop._measuredGeometry NAMES — EMULATE THE VIEWPORT INSTEAD. Measured 2026-09-08, re-confirmed 2026-09-27 (0.4.7) and re-derived 2026-09-29 for the NEW viewport of record against 0.4.11. 🔴 THE TRAP IS THAT TWO GATES READ DIFFERENT UNITS AND SATISFYING ONE BREAKS THE OTHER. `viewport_of_record` compares crop._measuredGeometry.viewport against the CAPTURE's pixel dimensions; `app_frame_scale` compares the PROBE's reading, which is CSS px × devicePixelRatio, against that same capture. `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` does NOT make window.devicePixelRatio return the overridden deviceScaleFactor — emulating the device figures at --dsf 1 satisfies `viewport_of_record` and then dies on `app_frame_scale`. ✅ THE SPELLING THAT WORKS: emulate in CSS px and let the scale factor carry the DPR, so both readings land on the same numbers — `browser --instance work --tab <id> emulate --width 1498 --height 1500 --dsf <live DPR>` (at the DPR measured today, 1.140625: 1498 × 1.140625 = 1708.7 → 1709; 1500 × 1.140625 = 1710.9 → 1711; the gates' tolerance is 2px). Confirmed end to end 2026-09-29: the probe answered APPFRAME_RECT:104,64,-1,1709,1711,0 and a raw CDP screenshot measured exactly 1709x1711. Then `capture.sh <recipe> --instance work --tab <id> --no-foreground`. 🔴 `--no-foreground` IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, NOT DIAGNOSTICS: an ACTIVE tab is captured by captureVisibleTab, which photographs real window pixels and IGNORES the emulation, so foregrounding silently re-introduces the mismatch. A tab opened by `browser open` is created inactive, which is what routes the capture onto CDP — and CDP honours the override. Confirm with `"via": "cdp"` in the screenshot op's answer. ⚠️ DERIVE --dsf FROM THE LIVE DISPLAY, DO NOT COPY 1.140625 — it is this operator's monitor today, not a constant; read devicePixelRatio and divide the recorded viewport by it. (2026-09-29: re-derived live from `window.devicePixelRatio`, still 1.140625 on a single 3440x1440 DP-0.) ⚠️ THE EMULATED HEIGHT IS NOT A FREE CHOICE ANY MORE and that is new for 0.4.11: it must leave the iframe taller than the tallest board or the app scrolls inside its own frame and a scrollbar returns — see `_iframeIsViewportCapped` for the 1263 CSS floor and the innerHeight-147 relationship. ⚠️ It also does NOT rescue the horizontal anchor: the live probe still answers leftInset=0 rightGap=-1, so this app IS still full-bleed and `xFrom`/`wFrom` remain ruled out for it — do not spend a session on that conversion. ✅ Evidence the y-anchor is earning its keep: appFrameTop moved 141 → 104 between the 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-08 readings and `yFrom: appFrame` absorbed it with no edit; it read 104 again on 2026-09-27 and again on 2026-09-29 at a viewport 456 device px taller.

CONTROLS: 'ZZZ-absent-sentinel' returned absent in all five, and 'Model Benchmarking' returned present in all five — so the matcher can report both values and the zeros above are not a broken check. ── 🔴 THE RETRACTION, AND IT IS THE ONE THE 0.4.7 NOTE PREDICTED IN WRITING. That note flagged 'Matchup' as unique only BY CASE and said: 'if any future version renders a title-case Matchups heading anywhere on the page, this discriminator goes INERT SILENTLY'. 0.4.11's board subnav renders exactly that — the segment labels are the literals 'Grids' / 'Matchups' / 'Prompts' (`BOARDS` in `BoardNav.tsx`) — so 'Matchup' is a substring of the always-present 'Matchups' and is now PRESENT IN ALL FIVE READS. It is INERT and has been removed. The prediction was right, the guard was not self-correcting, and the only thing that caught it was re-running the matrix. RE-RUN IT; DO NOT TRUST IT. A discriminator that has stopped discriminating looks identical to one that works — five identical screenshots and exit 0. ── 🔴 THE WEAKEST LINKS NOW, FLAGGED ON PURPOSE. The two modal discriminators are the modal TITLE followed by its CLOSE GLYPH across an innerText line break — 'Matchup' + newline + U+00D7, and 'Prompt' + newline + U+00D7. The titles alone cannot work (they are substrings of the subnav's 'Matchups' / 'Prompts', the same trap in a new spelling), and the modal BODIES carry no static text at all: the third IA pass deleted every badge from `MatchupBody.tsx`, so everything inside the matchup modal is dataset ('Illustrious · v9.0', a LoRA name). The newline is real — measured in the live `text` output — but it is a claim about how innerText joins a title to a sibling button, which no test in either repo pins. `prompt-detail` has a second, sturdier anchor ('Default (every ecosystem)', a structural label from `PromptBody`) and `matchup-detail` has no equivalent — an asymmetry that is real, not an omission. ⚠️ NEITHER IS ASSERTED ANY MORE: since 2026-09-30 the recipe uses the two modal needles ONLY as `waitForGone`, where the weakness runs the other way. A needle that has gone inert reports ABSENT, so an inert modal needle would silently stop guarding instead of loudly failing — which is why the matrix above must be RE-RUN rather than trusted. ── Why NOT a testid: `plan.py` emits `waitForText` as the `text` op with EMPTY argv, so the output is plain text with no attributes and a testid can never match. Selecting on the overlay's own `data-testid` would be the structurally better guard and the recipe form cannot express it. ── 🔴 THE NEEDLE IS MATCHED AGAINST THE BRIDGE'S RAW OUTPUT, NOT AGAINST THE DOM TEXT, AND THAT CHANGES HOW A NEWLINE MUST BE SPELLED. `capture.sh` does `case "$out" in *"$expect"*` where `$out` is the whole stdout+stderr of `browser --frame <f> text` — i.e. the bridge's JSON envelope, in which the page's newlines are already ESCAPED. Measured 2026-09-29 by reading the bytes: the raw output contains the two characters BACKSLASH and 'n' (not a newline) and the LITERAL 'U+00D7' character (not a \\u escape), so the two modal needles are written in this recipe as "Matchup\\n\u00d7" / "Prompt\\n\u00d7" — a JSON-escaped backslash followed by n. A needle containing a REAL newline cannot ever match. ✅ VERIFIED THROUGH THE REAL CODE PATH, not by reasoning about bash quoting: the plan's `expect` was extracted with capture.sh's own python one-liner (bytes `4d 61 74 63 68 75 70 5c 6e c3 97`) and fed to the same `case` statement — MATCH against the matchup-detail read, NO MATCH against the base read. Both controls in the same command. ⚠️ THE MATRIX ABOVE WAS ALSO RE-RUN AGAINST THE RAW OUTPUTS for this reason, not against the decoded text: an earlier pass of it used decoded text and would have shipped an unescaped needle that silently never matched. Every row above is a substring test on the exact bytes capture.sh sees.

That is the one thing `shelf-life-and-what-not-to-shoot.md` says to avoid and it is unavoidable in this form — a board has to show SOMETHING. ⚠️ AND ONE ROW IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN: the grids board's only card is badged YOURS and carries a `Remove` button, which is account state in the frame. Weigh that before listing the grids asset; the matchups and prompts assets do not have it.

ready._comment: 🔴 THE GATE IS `results-grid` BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY BOARD-INDEPENDENT LANDMARK DEEP ENOUGH TO MEAN 'BOOTED AND HAS DATA'. `BoardNav` mounts one board at a time and the unselected sections are ABSENT from the DOM, not hidden (asserted in the app repo's `src/boardNav.test.tsx`), so any `section-*` gate stops existing the moment a state clicks another segment — that is what makes a section gate wrong here, not that it is broken. `results-grid` lives inside `section-open-grid`, which `App.tsx` renders on Home WHICHEVER board is selected, and it exists only once the open grid's matrix has resolved. ── 🔴 IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT `app-content` OR `app-surface`: both are the outer shell and would go true before the grid exists, which is the too-early gate this mechanism exists to prevent — a click fired into a still-booting app is DISCARDED and the NEXT wait times out naming the wrong control, so the run reports a defect in a component that is perfectly fine. That misdiagnosis has cost a session in this recipe's own history. ── ✅ IT COVERS EVERY TRIGGER, BY STRUCTURE RATHER THAN CONTAINMENT. `board-nav-matchups` and `board-nav-prompts` are not inside `results-grid`, but `BoardNav` is rendered in the same `view.kind === 'home'` branch as `section-open-grid` in `App.tsx`, so if `results-grid` resolved, `board-nav` is mounted. VERIFIED LIVE rather than only read: after a `nav` to the app URL, a poll of the app frame every 2s from +2s to +12s found `results-grid`, `board-nav`, `section-open-grid`, `section-grids`, `grid-group-matchup` and `grid-col-header` present at EVERY sample. ── ⚠️ `loadingTestid` is `app-loading`, which the served bundle carries (count 1) — but `app-loading` was ABSENT at every one of those samples, having already resolved before the first read. It is declared on the bundle's evidence and NOT on an observation of the loading state itself. Say so rather than treating it as verified. ── 🔴 BUT THE GATE IS NOT CONTENT-INDEPENDENT, AND THIS IS THE FIRST PLACE TO LOOK WHEN IT TIMES OUT. `ResultsGrid.tsx:246` EARLY-RETURNS an `EmptyState` (`grid-empty`) whenever `configs.length === 0 || prompts.length === 0`, and `results-grid` is rendered below that return (`:286`) — so on an open grid whose `configs` or `prompts` resolve EMPTY — which is wider than 'lost its last matchup': `configs` comes from `flattenConfigs` (`lib/benchmark.ts:920`), which pushes one row per `combo.data.configs` entry and so returns `[]` when every included matchup carries NO model config, matchups present. The other arm is losing the last included prompt, `results-grid` NEVER MOUNTS and this gate stalls its full 45s. The old `section-grids` gate had no such dependency: it mounted whenever `board === 'grids'`. It fails CLOSED (no asset ships), so the cost is diagnosis, not a wrong capture — but the boot-timing history above will send you at the wrong file. CHECK FOR `grid-empty` IN THE FRAME FIRST; if it is there the app is fine and the BOARD is empty.

_howToDismissal: 🔴 THE FIRST ACTION OF EVERY STATE IS PROFILE-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS `clickIfPresent` AND NOT `click`. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS across reloads (see `_noExplainerState`), so `[data-testid='howto-dismiss']` exists on a profile that has never run this app and is ABSENT on every profile that has. Re-measured 2026-09-29 on live 0.4.11: `howto-dismiss` is present in the served bundle (count 2) and the string 'How this works' is in the bundle (count 1) — but BOTH are absent from the live DOM and from all five whole-frame text reads on this operator's profile, so here the `clickIfPresent` skips and the `waitForGone` is satisfied instantly. Both are correct, and neither may be the only supported one: deleting the click breaks a fresh profile, while leaving it a plain `click` makes the bridge's `element_not_found` an action FAILURE on a used one. The `waitForGone` that follows is NOT dead and must stay: a wait-until-absent is satisfied instantly when the panel is already gone, and on a fresh profile it is the only thing stopping the next click from racing the dismissal. ⚠️ It is therefore VACUOUS on this profile — it proves nothing here, and that is not a reason to delete it.

_mutualExclusion: 🔴 EVERY STATE ASSERTS ITS OWN SURFACE IS OPEN *AND* THAT THE OTHERS ARE CLOSED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS NOT SYMMETRY FOR ITS OWN SAKE — IT IS A DEFECT THAT HAS SHIPPED INTO AN ASSET. ── THE MECHANISM, STATED ONCE, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: `capture.sh` reloads the app before every state EXCEPT THE FIRST ('the first state already landed'), so state 1 inherits whatever the tab was left in. Any run passing `--tab <id>` of a tab someone has been clicking in is exposed; a tab `capture.sh` opens itself is not. 🔴 THE OPERATIONAL RULE THAT FOLLOWS: a `--tab` you have been reading or clicking in is DIRTY — `nav` it to the app URL before the run, every time. ── THE INCIDENT LEDGER, THREE ENTRIES, SAME MECHANISM: (1) 2026-09-27, the one that shipped — a full run exited 0, passed store-bounds, and produced an asset showing the Contribute dropdown AND a leftover Prompt detail panel open together. The single `waitForText` was satisfied (the string really was on screen), so nothing in the pipeline objected. CAUGHT BY EYE, NOT BY A GATE — which is why the guard exists. (2) 2026-09-29, by accident, after the guard — a single-state re-run fired at a tab the previous run had left on an open `prompt-detail` modal died on `TIMEOUT waiting for absence of Prompt\n\u00d7`, exit 4, NO ASSET SHIPPED. Without the `waitForGone` it would have exited 0 with a prompt modal over the grids board: incident (1), reproduced two days later. (3) 2026-09-30, by accident again, in a DIFFERENT SHAPE — the re-shoot was fired at a tab driven by hand onto the PROMPTS board while the crop was being measured; `grids-board` inherited it and died at step [4] on `TIMEOUT waiting for A grid is a named set of matchups`, exit 4, NO ASSET SHIPPED. 🔴 NOTE WHICH HALF CAUGHT IT: not a `waitForGone` but the state's OWN `waitForText`, because the contaminant was another BOARD rather than a modal. THE PAIR IS THE POINT — asserting only 'my surface is open' misses (2); asserting only 'the others are closed' misses (3). ── WHAT EACH STATE ASSERTS, AND WHY IT IS CHEAP. Each board state asserts the OTHER TWO BOARDS are unmounted — a claim `BoardNav` makes exact, because the unselected boards are ABSENT from the DOM, not hidden (the app repo asserts that by absence in `src/boardNav.test.tsx`, deliberately, because `display: none` would satisfy a visibility check while leaving every testid resolving). Each also asserts BOTH detail modals are closed; those surfaces still exist in the app and are still reachable by hand even though no state photographs them since 2026-09-30. Measured 2026-09-29: opening one detail modal closes the other, and a board click opens neither. ── ⚠️ 'THEY ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE' WAS TOO NARROW A READING ONCE ALREADY — true of the pair tested, false of the pair not tested (the Contribute dropdown happily coexisted with a detail panel). That menu is gone; the lesson is why every state asserts every OTHER surface rather than the one it was observed to conflict with. ── WHY THE GUARD IS RIGHT RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND: it pins a RELATIONSHIP (this surface open, those closed) instead of a single word, so it fails LOUDLY — `waitForGone` polls until absent and then times out as an action failure (exit 4) naming the string — rather than silently photographing two surfaces. It does NOT repair a dirty tab and is not meant to; it converts a silent wrong-screen capture into a stopped run. ⚠️ IT IS VACUOUS ON A CLEAN RUN, which is exactly why it must not be deleted as dead weight.
_statesRebuilt: 🔴 THREE STATES, ONE PER BOARD, AND THE SET IS DELIBERATELY NOT LARGER. It was five until 2026-09-30: the three boards plus a `matchup-detail` and a `prompt-detail` modal. Those two were dropped because THE LIVE STORE GALLERY IS THREE SHOTS and the detail assets mapped to none of them — they were invented for 0.4.7 as substitutes *because* the boards were unphotographable then, a premise `_iframeIsViewportCapped` killed. 🔴 THE RULE THIS LEAVES: IF THE LISTING TAKES ONLY THREE, TAKE THE THREE BOARDS. ── ⚠️ THE ASSETS' DIFFERENTIATION, HONESTLY, AND IT IS WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS. The three boards share the open-grid panel across their top 608 CSS px and differ only below the subnav — roughly the bottom 43% of each asset (⚠️ the 608 CSS px was MEASURED in `cc64fbad8b` and CARRIED ACROSS the h change by `bb991fa8b6`, whose message claims no measurement was carried over — that is the commit the retraction is against, not cc64fbad8b, which measured it. 🔴 BUT NOT ON THE AXIS AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE NAMED: `h` is NOT a render parameter. `frame.py:1314` `render_argv` emits `-crop WxH+X+Y` against the ALREADY-CAPTURED PNG, and both candidates were framed from captures at the same `_viewportOfRecord` and the same `APPFRAME_RECT`, so h=1428 and h=1224 are two post-hoc crops of ONE unchanged layout and 608 CANNOT differ between them. Only the denominator moved. 608's staleness risk is against a FUTURE APP-LAYOUT change, not against this crop — and 48.6%/56.7% do NOT inherit an h-related uncertainty. 608/1073 frame-CSS is 57% shared, so the DIFFERING band is 43%, not a third). They are less different from each other than the 0.4.6 tab panels were. 🔴 A DECLARED RECT MAKES THE IDENTICAL-BOX CHECK INERT, so NOTHING in this pipeline will tell you if they collapse into near-duplicates; that judgement is BY EYE, every time, and it is the only check there is. ── ⚠️ A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING: the shared top 57% means any content defect in the open-grid matrix appears in ALL THREE assets at once. The one empty cell reading `not generated yet` / `Run this cell` is exactly that, and filling it would SPEND THE VIEWER'S OWN BUZZ — see `_contentCaveat`.
_noExplainerState: 🔴 There is deliberately NO `explainer` state, and it is not an oversight. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS (it does not come back on reload), so the first state that dismisses [data-testid='howto-dismiss'] destroys it for every later state in the same run — the explainer state was tried last and captured nothing, because by then it was gone. Capturing it needs a profile that has never dismissed it, which this scripted path cannot arrange. custom-generators' recipe gets away with an `explainer` state only because it is listed FIRST. Do not 'fix' this by reordering: every state dismisses it as its first action, so whichever runs first still kills it.
